analysis:
Integration of the two prior analyses and the replayed changelog and docs units; the replay was incomplete (361 omitted units), so the Swift sources were not directly verified.

Reported (low): the VerifiedWeightHashStore (`~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json`) lets registration reuse a weight hash on matching stat metadata (changelog.d/glm-startup-single-verification.md:4). The operator is the adversary in T-012 and T-027, so a stat-keyed, owner-only record is not an integrity proof. I cite the changelog line because it is the visible evidence. The store implementation and registration gating (`weightsVerifiedByManagedLoad`) were not seen.

Not reported: unit 0's SystemMemory reclaimable-policy finding (over-admission is availability-only and carries no threat ID), as its source lines are not in the replay and cannot be verified here. Unit 1 found no supported regression.

Unverified contracts:
- GLM managed-load SHA-256 verification of every manifest file before serving, with failure on a changed file identity. The changelog claims it and the tests reportedly support it.
- The GLM json_schema, forced tool_choice and strict-tool paths withhold output until validation. They must stay fail-closed with content-free 422 errors (A-001, T-008).
- GLM5NextWiredLimitNotice logging only fixed text with no request-derived content.
- nativeOutputControlRefusal returns 400 before any reservation, so it stays out of breaker strikes (T-010).
- The variable-frame-rate video bounds (T-050) and the mlx-swift-lm submodule bump.

T-041 SSD cache code was not touched.

findings.detail: The changelog (changelog.d/glm-startup-single-verification.md line 4) describes a new `~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json` record. Coordinator-mode start registers the recorded hash while each weight file keeps its device, inode, size, mtime and ctime. The only protection stated is 'owner-only', and the owner is the provider operator (ADV-001). The operator could write a record for substituted weights, or edit weights and restore their stat metadata. Registration would then publish the earlier verified hash without re-reading the bytes. This narrows the weight-substitution control (T-012/T-027) and adds an operator-writable trust input. The registered hash was already self-reported, so this is a threat-model gap rather than a proven bypass. The model should record that this cache is self-attested local state, not an integrity proof. If it is meant as a control, MAC-bind it to the SE-rooted KEK. The implementation was not supplied, so the contract is unverified.
findings.title: Weight-hash verification cache keyed on stat metadata with no stated integrity protection
